items.title: Record Drawings
items.stakes: Wes calls from Brackenmoor: the East Wing's record drawings are fiction in at least one clinic room — and the fiction started on a sheet Maya drew.
items.reward: Record drawings a technician can trust, and a mistake owned where it started.

objectives.text: Find what the record set was drawn from
Decide what to do about your own sheet
Look closer: two things about the East Wing

items.rumor: Everyone did their job right except the drawing that said what everyone had done.

items.alt: Priya at her desk on a video call with Wes, from Brackenmoor, on screen.

bubbles.text: Your East Wing record drawings say clinic room 4 has twelve ports. It has six. One is the nurse-call panel.

items.caption: A technician nearly patched a display into it. The label stopped him.

lines.text: Nobody's hurt. The panel's label stopped him. I'd just like to know how many other rooms are wrong.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #60 · AVERY'S LENS  Document what's there, not what was meant  A record of how something was meant to be is a plan; a record of how it is — checked in the room — is what the next person can trust.  The East Wing's record drawings recorded the design. The room recorded something else, and a technician nearly trusted the drawing.

items.alt: The record drawing for clinic room 4: twelve grey port boxes, D1 to D12, noted ‘drawn from the design set’.
items.caption: Twelve ports on paper.

items.prompt: Nadia would've walked every room before she believed a drawing. I'm trying to be her. Coming?

options.label: “On my way. Can we bring clinical engineering for the nurse-call ports?”
options.reply: Already asked. They said thanks for asking.

options.label: “I'll fix the drawings from here.”
options.reply: From the design set? That's what's wrong.

options.label: “How many rooms have you checked?”
options.reply: One. Room 4. That's why I'm calling.

hints.text: What's actually in the room — and who owns the clinical port?

options.label: Send corrected drawings from the office tonight
options.result: Corrected from the design set — the thing that was wrong.
options.consequence: An office fix of an office mistake.

options.result: Six outlets, nurse call on D5 — and the record set was drawn from the design, not the redlines.

options.label: Tell Wes which port to patch the display into
options.result: Wes: “Clinical engineering owns anything near that panel. We don't patch from a guess.”

options.result: The contractor installed exactly the clinical layout. Correctly.

items.title: Blueprints
items.body: In 1842 the astronomer John Herschel invented the cyanotype — paper that turns blue where light reaches it. By the 1870s engineering offices were using it to copy drawings: white lines on blue, every copy identical to the master. The word ‘blueprint’ outlived the process. The lesson didn't change: a copy is only as true as the drawing it was made from.

hints.text: What evidence should a record drawing come from?

options.label: Every record set is drawn from redlines and a room-by-room field check, signed off, with clinical and life-safety ports marked for their owners — and copied rooms re-checked at every revision
options.result: Priya adds a field-verified sign-off to the handover checklist.

options.label: Draw record sets from the design, carefully
options.result: The design is exactly what changes on site.

options.label: Never copy rooms
options.result: Kit spends three days drawing identical rooms by hand.
options.consequence: Copying isn't the fault; not re-checking is.

options.label: Nothing — the East Wing is fixed
options.result: The courthouse record set is next month.

items.sub: Intermediate · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Priya and Maya beside a board. A ratio is one cost over another. Fixing a line on a drawing is one; fixing it on site is about ten; fixing it after people move in, about a hundred. So the port map error costs a hundred times what it would have in design. Rule of thumb, not a law. But it's why we check drawings against the building.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  Record drawings come from what was built: the contractor’s redlines and a room-by-room field check, signed off. Mark clinical and life-safety ports for their owners. When the mistake is yours, say so — then find every place it went. Design : site : occupancy ≈ 1 : 10 : 100 (rule of thumb).
REFLECTION (optional)  · Maya found her own week-two mistake in week thirty. What would you want to find in your own old work — before someone else does?
